Problem Statement
You are given a 2D grid of size n \times m, representing a map of tasks. Each cell (i, j) contains an integer A[i][j]:
If A[i][j] > 0, it represents the time required to complete the work at that specific grid cell.
If A[i][j] = 0, the cell is empty (no work is required, but it can be traversed).
You start from a given starting position (or choose your starting position depending on the variant) and can move to any adjacent cell (up, down, left, right).
Each movement between two adjacent cells costs a fixed time of 2 units, regardless of whether the target cell has work or is empty (0).
To complete the work at a cell, you must spend the full work time specified by A[i][j] at that cell. Work at a cell is completed only once.
Your objective is to find the minimum total time required to visit and complete the work across the required cells

You are given a string N. Your task is to reverse the string while keeping the spaces in their original positions, followed by the total count of the words in the string.

A single line contains an input string N.

1 <= N <= 10^6

A single line containing the modified string, and the word count at the end.

my name is doselect

Reverse the characters of the string without changing the positions of the spaces.

10 seconds

You are given an n x n chessboard with the positions of a knight and a queen.

- Diagonally

text: has anyone appeared for rubrik offcampus 6M intern OA?
media.net oa questions?

The online assessment process consisted of two rounds focused heavily on Linux, systems, networking, and server-side concepts. In the first round, candidates worked on practical Linux-based tasks directly through the terminal, making it important to be comfortable with basic Linux commands, file editing, and system administration concepts. The questions were primarily server- and protocol-oriented, including tasks such as changing a server's port number when it was misconfigured, identifying and fixing missing port configurations, editing files exclusively through the terminal, and correcting syntax errors in Python files using command-line tools. A large number of students participated, and around sixty candidates advanced to the next stage.

The second round was another online assessment, for which participants were required to set up a Linux environment, either by installing WSL/Linux on their personal machines or by using the laboratory computers. This round was entirely server-focused and involved implementing practical networking applications. The first task required building a UDP echo server, while the second involved creating a key-value store supporting operations such as setting, retrieving, and updating values. Additional tasks covered multithreading concepts, and one of the later problems involved communication between nodes, likely using a gossip-based mechanism. Detailed documentation was provided for each task, so candidates were not expected to work completely from scratch; however, a solid understanding of socket programming was essential. The choice of programming language was not a significant hurdle. After completing the assessment, interviewers interacted individually with candidates, asking questions about their implementations and problem-solving approaches before recording their evaluations and remarks.
